props.heading: What We Do

props.body:
PureHeart Islamic Foundation of Nigeria (PHF), Lagos State Chapter, is a da'wah and welfare organisation dedicated to the holistic development of Muslim youth, students and women.

Through structured programmes, community outreach and a network of 11 active branches across Lagos, we work to raise principled leaders and strengthen the fabric of the Muslim community in Lagos State.

props.intro: Whether you want to attend a programme, volunteer your skills or support our work, getting involved with PHF Lagos is straightforward.

items.title: Find Your Local Branch
items.description: Locate the PHF branch closest to you and connect directly with your branch coordinator via WhatsApp.

items.title: Attend a Programme
items.description: Register for any of our six programmes through your branch coordinator or reach out to the secretariat for details.

items.title: Volunteer or Donate
items.description: Offer your time across one of our six departments, or donate to support our welfare and da'wah work across Lagos.

props.heading: Three Ways to Join the PHF Community

items.answer: We have 11 branches across Lagos including Ikorodu, Kosofe, Ikeja, Surulere, Ojo, Badagry, Isolo, Mushin, Alimosho and Apapa. Visit our Branches page to find your coordinator's WhatsApp contact.
items.question: How do I find my nearest PHF branch?

items.answer: Programme registration is handled through your local branch coordinator. Find your branch coordinator on the Branches page and reach out to them directly via WhatsApp.
items.question: How can I register for a programme?

items.answer: You can volunteer across six departments: Media & Publicity, Welfare & Outreach, Logistics & Events, Da'wah & Education, Finance & Sponsorship, and Sisters' Affairs. Use the Volunteer form on our website to indicate your interest and your message will be sent to the State Coordinator.
items.question: How do I volunteer with PHF Lagos?

items.answer: Donations are accepted via bank transfer to: Account Name – Pure Heart Islamic Foundation of Nigeria (PHF), Account No – 1100277183, Bank – Al-Barakah MFB. Please reach out to us after transferring so we can acknowledge your support.

entries.title: How clean water changed school attendance in Ikorodu

cover.alt: A bustling aerial view of Lagos, Nigeria showcasing dense urban architecture and busy traffic.
cover.credit: Photo by Taiwo Samson on Pexels

data.title: How clean water changed school attendance in Ikorodu
data.author: Amaka Obi, Programmes Lead
data.excerpt: When the nearest borehole is 3 km away, girls miss school to fetch water. Here’s what happened when we brought water to the school gate.
data.seoTitle: Clean water and school attendance in Ikorodu | HopeBridge Foundation
data.seoDescription: How a single borehole helped keep more girls in school in Ikorodu, Lagos, and how you can help us reach the next community.

entries.body:
For many families on the edge of Ikorodu, the day starts with a walk. Before school, before breakfast, someone has to fetch water, and that someone is usually a girl.

The problem

At Ebute Community Primary School, the nearest safe water point was a 40-minute walk away. Teachers told us that on many mornings, a third of the girls in Primary 5 arrived late or not at all.

  • Children walked up to 3 km each way to collect water

  • The school had no water for handwashing or toilets

  • Diarrhoea and stomach illness were a common reason for absence

What we did

Working with the school’s parent–teacher association and local leaders, we installed a solar-powered borehole and three handwashing stations at the school gate. Parents formed a water committee to manage maintenance and keep the area clean.

What changed

Within one term, teachers reported that morning lateness dropped noticeably, and fewer children were sent home sick. More importantly, girls who used to spend their mornings carrying water were now in class.

“My daughter used to cry because she was always late. Now she is the first one at school.” — a parent at Ebute

What’s next

There are four more schools in the area without safe water. Each borehole costs about ₦4.5 million to install, and the community commits to maintaining it.

How you can help

You can sponsor a handwashing station, fund part of a borehole, or volunteer with our community health team. Every contribution goes directly to the next school on our list.
